full_judgment:
Md. Gholam Rabbani J: This Rule questions the extent of the discretion of the Courts to add third party as defendant in a suit. This judicial discretion given in sub-rule 2, rule10, Order 1, CPC is required to be set at right as we are experiencing now-a-days trial Court's lack of judicial consideration while allowing or disallowing an application of a third party for adding him as defendant in a suit. 

 "The Court may at any stage of the proceedings, either upon or without the application of either party, and on such terms as may appear to the Court to be just, order that the name of any party improperly joined, whether as plaintiff or defendant, be struck out, and that the name of any person who ought to have been joined, whether as plaintiff or defendant, or whose presence before the Court may be necessary in order to enable the Court effectually and completely to adjudicate upon and settle all the questions involved in the suit, be added." 

 "The Court may at any stage of the proceeding upon the application of party, on such term as may appear to be just, order that the name of any person who ought to have been joined as defendant or whose presence before the Court may be necessary in order to enable the Court effectually and completely to adjudicate upon and settle all the questions involved in the suit, be added." 

 "The Court  may order that the name of any person (a) who ought to have been joined as defendant or (b) whose presence before the Court may be necessary in order to enable the Court effectually and completely to adjudicate upon and settle all the questions in the suit, be added." 

 9. Now we come to consider the persons falling in category (b). This is the difficult part. Who are the persons whose presence are necessary in order to enable the Court effectually and completely adjudicate upon and settle all the questions involved in the suit? 

 11. Take a suit for partition of the joint family properties. A third party wants to be added as a defendant claiming an item of the suit properties as his own. He is a necessary party. Insofar as the decision whether this item of property will or will not be available for partition is concerned the question involved is no longer between the parties to the suit alone, but between also this third party. So also a third party is a necessary party in a partition suit disputing altogether the title of the plaintiff, but admitting the defendants as his co-owners. A court can pass a decree for partition among the defendants even dismissing the plaintiff's claim. A third party will be a necessary party in a partition suit when he denies the title of both the plaintiffs and defendants to the suit property. 

 15. In view of the discussion as above the question of addition of an intervener in a suit as necessary party under Order 1, rule 10, sub-rule 2, we find, is not one of initial jurisdiction of the court, but of a judicial discretion which has to be exercised in terms of this sub-rule. In order to be impleaded in a suit the third party must have a legal interest as distinguished from a commercial interest, that is, assertion of the third party that his addition will avoid multiplicity of suits or will be convenient for the purpose of trial or will not cause prejudice to any party will not be of any avail. He must be legally interested in the answers to the issues in the suit, that is, it will affect or curtail his legal right. And what are issues to be answered in a suit (p) To find out them the averments in the plaint alone should be looked into. 

 16. Now we consider the instant civil revision. Plaint case briefly, is this. Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate was the owner of the suit property at the time of C S operation. Anand Lal Dhupi took pattan thereof on 24-5-32. By an unregistered deed of sale dated 1-1-43 Ananda sold the property to Nazrul Islam who accordingly possessed the same and got his name recorded in RS Khatian. Plaintiff purchased the suit property from Nazrul Islam by a registered sale deed on 5-7-93. Thus the plaintiff is now the owner of the suit property, but the defendants are trying to lease out the same. Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate, Dhaka Division Commissioner and Chairman of Land Reform Board are the defendants in the suit. 

 17. It appears from the application dated 25-10-94 of the opposite party Nos.1 to 7 under Order 1, rule 10, sub-rule 2, CPC that there are at least seven shop rooms in the suit property, that the applicants took sub-lease of the shop rooms each separately from the plaintiff on the understanding that the plaintiff had taken lease of the property from the Court of Wards Estate, that the said lease of the plaintiff was cancelled on 17-2-94 by the Land Reforms Board and that two years before the applicants applied for granting them lease of their respective shop rooms. 

 20. In view of the legal position as discussed above, the allegation made in the plaint and the allegations made in the application for addition of parties we do not find that the said opposite parties arc necessary parties in this suit. The issue involved in the suit is whether the plaintiff has title to the suit property or whether the suit property is the Khas property of Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate and to adjudicate the issue presence of the opposite parties in not necessary. A court has jurisdiction to add as defendant a person even when a plaintiff does not wish to sue him only in a case where the plaintiff is seeking a relief which may directly affect the intervener by curtailing the enjoyment of his legal rights and consequently his presence is "necessary to enable the court to adjudicate completely and effectually upon and settle all the questions involved in the suit."
